attributes.residual: ONE ours-only `addi` at @0x30 and one schedule-class loop-base placement. Named mechanism: the target emits `add r31,r3,r4` (cp IS the address expression's destination) then `addi r30,r31,0` (p = a chained copy of cp), two instructions. We emit `add r3,r3,r4` into a VOLATILE temp then TWO copies from it, `addi r31,r3,0` and `addi r30,r3,0`, three instructions. MWCC copy-propagates our `p = cp` back to the shared CSE temp T, so cp and p become two independent consumers of T and T needs its own register; in the target the second copy reads cp's register instead. Every other register role now matches the target exactly, including `stmw r28,112(r1)` (four callee-saved, up from three), r29=i, r31=cheat-block pointer, r30=post-cheat pointer, r28=lvl. NEXT LANE: the open question is narrow and named - how to spell `p = cp` so MWCC's copy propagation does NOT see through it to T. The u8* cast-transit on `p` fixes the COLOURING (real 295 -> 147) but not the temp; the same cast on `cp` is measured harmful (real 147 -> 295, axis3). Do not re-run axis1, axis3, or the lvl/exp/product initializer lever.
